question: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b: Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line allows passing from the side with the broken line, provided it is safe.

question: What does a chemical test measure?
options: a: Reaction time.,b: Blood alcohol content.,c: Vision.
note: A chemical test measures blood alcohol content (BAC) to determine the level of alcohol in a driver's system.

question: A child passenger under 8 and shorter than ___ in height is required to be seated in an approved child safety seat while in a moving vehicle.
options: a: 4 feet 11 inches,b: 5 feet,c: 5 feet 5 inches
note: New York law requires children under 8 and shorter than 4 feet 9 inches to use an approved child safety seat.

question: What does a red painted curb mean?
options: a: No parking standing or stopping.,b: The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c: Loading zone.
note: A red painted curb indicates no parking, standing, or stopping is allowed, typically for safety or emergency access.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?
options: a: A road hazard sign.,b: Interstate route sign.,c: School crossing sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used to warn drivers of road hazards, such as curves, intersections, or other potential dangers.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicates?
options: a: Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe.,c: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not permitted for either direction.

question: If a driver is approaching a flashing red traffic signal they must:
options: a: Slow down.,b: Drive carefully without stopping.,c: Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red traffic signal requires drivers to come to a complete stop, treating it like a stop sign.

section-name: Passing, Lane Changes, and Speed Management
question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?
options: a: On a narrow bridge.,b: If it means driving off the pavement.,c: Even if the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
note: Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and there is an available passing lane, provided it is safe.

question: A driver may park in a space reserved for people with disabilities:
options: a: Only if the driver is disabled.,b: Regardless of who is in the vehicle.,c: Is carrying the disabled person named on the registration.
note: Parking in a disabled space is allowed only when transporting the disabled person named on the registration or permit.

question: What should a driver do if they are taking a non-prescription drug?
options: a: Should read the labels on the drug before driving.,b: Drink alcohol instead.,c: Continue driving regardless of any warning labels.
note: Drivers should read labels on non-prescription drugs to check for warnings about driving impairment.

question: What contains the same amount of alcohol as a five-ounce glass of wine?
options: a: A gallon of wine.,b: One 12-ounce can of beer.,c: One pint of whiskey.
note: A 12-ounce can of beer (5% alcohol) contains roughly the same amount of alcohol as a 5-ounce glass of wine (12% alcohol).

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection mean?
options: a: A stop sign.,b: A yield sign.,c: A slow sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal functions as a stop sign, requiring a complete stop before proceeding.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a: Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,b: Slow down and proceed with caution.,c: Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution, yielding to other traffic.

question: What can a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph could take _______ to come to a complete stop?
options: a: 400 feet,b: 125 feet,c: 50 feet
note: A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph can require up to 400 feet to stop due to its weight and momentum.

question: A large truck is in front of you and is making right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:
options: a: Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.,b: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
note: Large trucks often need to swing wide to complete turns, especially right turns, due to their size and turning radius.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: What should a motorist do when approaching a bicyclist?
options: a: Speed up to pass them.,b: Proceed.,c: Turn into the opposite lane.
note: Motorists should proceed cautiously when approaching a bicyclist, maintaining a safe distance and passing only when safe.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: A motorist should be aware that a bicyclist riding on the roadway must:
options: a: Ride on the right side of the road.,b: Ride on either side of the road.,c: Ride on the side of the road facing traffic.
note: Bicyclists must ride on the right side of the road, in the same direction as traffic, per traffic laws.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: What should you do when a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle?
options: a: Flash your lights.,b: Slow down.,c: Speed up and pass the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must slow down and yield to pedestrians crossing in front of their vehicle for safety.

section-name: Passing, Lane Changes, and Speed Management
question: A person who drives much slower than the posted speed limit: That person:
options: a: Always has the right-of-way.,b: Is a very safe driver.,c: Should not allow following cars to pass.
note: Driving significantly slower than the speed limit can impede traffic, and such drivers should allow others to pass when safe.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?
options: a: Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,b: Look both ways as you cross the intersection.,c: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red and white triangular sign is a yield sign, requiring drivers to look both ways and yield to other traffic or pedestrians.

question: What has a same meaning as a red flashing traffic light?
options: a: Solid red light.,b: Yield sign.,c: Stop sign.
note: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a stop sign, requiring a complete stop.

question: What does a regulatory sign containing a red circle with a slash through the middle indicates?
options: a: Drivers should come to a complete stop.,b: An action is forbidden.,c: Some drivers should yield to other drivers.
note: A red circle with a slash indicates a prohibited action, such as 'No Left Turn' or 'No U-Turn.'

question: What is the symbol of a slow-moving vehicle?
options: a: A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,b: A circular green sign.,c: A rectangular red sign.
note: A slow-moving vehicle is marked by a rectangular red or orange sign with a reflective border, typically on vehicles like farm equipment.

question: What does a solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants in to the left shows?
options: a: You are approaching a construction area.,b: There is an intersection just ahead.,c: You will be required to turn left just ahead.
note: A solid white line slanting left on the right edge of the highway indicates an upcoming intersection.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a: Do not pass.,b: Traffic light ahead.,c: Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline prohibits passing from your direction.

section-name: Passing, Lane Changes, and Speed Management
question: What is a speed limit?
options: a: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,b: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,c: The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on a road under ideal conditions, though drivers must adjust for safety.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a: Adjust your mirrors.,b: Increase your speed.,c: You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed only if is safe.
note: A steady green light allows drivers to proceed through the intersection at a safe speed, provided it is clear.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal light is a warning that the light is about to change to red. What should you do if you are already within the intersection when a green light changes to yellow?
options: a: Stop.,b: Increase your speed.,c: Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
note: If already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drivers should continue moving to clear it safely.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that a ______ light will soon appear.
options: a: Steady red.,b: Steady green.,c: Flashing yellow.
note: A steady yellow light warns that a steady red light, requiring a stop, will soon appear.

question: What is the symbol of a stop sign?
options: a: Rectangle.,b: Square.,c: Circle.
note: A stop sign is an octagon, often referred to as a square with cut corners, for easy recognition.

question: What does a traffic light mean when displaying a green arrow and a red light?
options: a: You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,b: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,c: You may only drive straight ahead.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows driving only in the direction of the arrow, such as a left or right turn.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: When can you proceed after stopping for a school bus that is unloading children?
options: a: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,b: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c: Accelerate quickly.
note: After stopping for a school bus, drivers must watch for children and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Alcohol is:
options: a: A stimulant.,b: An antihistamine.,c: A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant, slowing down the central nervous system and impairing driving ability.

question: Always allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:
options: a: Passenger vehicle.,b: Station wagon.,c: Motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles require extra following distance due to their ability to stop quickly and their vulnerability.

question: When an approaching driver fails to dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?
options: a: Toward the left side of the road.,b: Toward the right side of the road.,c: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
note: To avoid glare from high beams, look toward the right side of the road to stay oriented.

question: Who is an inattentive driver?
options: a: Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.,b: Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.,c: Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is distracted by staring off the roadway or daydreaming, reducing awareness of traffic.

question: What should you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a: Slow down and proceed with caution.,b: Stop before crossing the intersection.,c: Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light requires slowing down and proceeding cautiously, yielding to other traffic.

question: As you are close to an intersection the traffic light changes from green to yellow. Your best action is to:
options: a: Speed up to beat the red light.,b: Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.,c: Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
note: When a light turns yellow near an intersection, apply the brakes to stop safely, avoiding entering the intersection.

question: What should you do after you have finished parallel parking in a space between two other cars and assuming the street is level?
options: a: Move as far forward in the space as possible.,b: Make sure your car almost touches the car behind you.,c: Leave your front wheels turned toward the curb.
note: After parallel parking on a level street, leave front wheels turned toward the curb to prevent rolling.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: At a crosswalk:
options: a: Yield to pedestrians.,b: Pedestrians must yield to you.,c: Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at crosswalks to ensure their safety.

question: You may proceed in the direction of the arrow at a red traffic light with a green arrow if:
options: a: Come to a complete stop.,b: Wait until the light changes.,c: You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows proceeding in the arrow’s direction if in the correct lane and the road is clear.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?
options: a: Watch for children and be ready to stop.,b: Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c: Always honk your horn when you see children.
note: At a school crossing sign, watch for children and be prepared to stop to ensure their safety.

question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast day?
options: a: Not turn on any vehicle lights.,b: Drive using your parking lights.,c: Drive using your four-way flashers.
note: At dusk or on overcast days, use low-beam headlights (not parking lights or flashers) for visibility.

question: What is hard to see at night?
options: a: Pedestrians.,b: Road signs.,c: Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are hard to see at night due to low visibility, requiring extra caution.

section-name: Passing, Lane Changes, and Speed Management
question: What should you do before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle?
options: a: Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b: Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c: All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, check blind spots, mirrors, and signal your intention.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a: Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,b: Buckle your safety belt.,c: Both of the above.
note: Before starting the vehicle, ensure both you and your passengers are buckled up.

question: What should you do before turning?
options: a: Increase your speed.,b: Turn the wheel.,c: Use your signal.
note: Signal your intention to turn well in advance to alert other drivers.

question: What should you do before leaving a parking space that is parallel to the curb?
options: a: Use your horn.,b: Turn on your four-way flashers.,c: Look for traffic by turning your head.
note: Before leaving a parallel parking space, check for traffic by turning your head to ensure it’s safe.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: What does bicyclists aren’t required to if they differ from motorists?
options: a: Report accidents resulting in serious injury.,b: Signal all turns.,c: Obey the same traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists are not required to signal all turns, unlike motorists, but must still follow most traffic laws.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: Blind persons legally have the right-of-way when crossing the street when they are:
options: a: Helped by another person.,b: Led by a guide dog or using a white or metallic cane.,c: Wearing light-colored clothing.
note: Blind persons have the right-of-way when using a guide dog or white/metallic cane, indicating their need for priority.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a: Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b: Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c: Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas around a vehicle not visible in mirrors, requiring drivers to check physically.

question: What does a construction zone sign look like?
options: a: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b: Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Construction zone signs are typically diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors for high visibility.

question: What happens when you continuously hard brake on ice and snow?
options: a: Helps you stop faster.,b: Keeps the brakes from freezing.,c: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle causing a loss of steering.
note: Hard braking on ice or snow can lock the wheels, causing a loss of steering control.

question: What does a crossbuck sign indicate?
options: a: Railroad crossings.,b: School zones.,c: No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck sign indicates a railroad crossing, warning drivers to be cautious.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a: Defending yourself against drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,b: Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c: Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving involves anticipating hazards and taking actions to avoid accidents.

question: What can cause distracted driving?
options: a: Changing a CD.,b: Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,c: Eating drinking or smoking.
note: Talking or texting on a phone is a significant cause of distracted driving, reducing focus on the road.

question: You should not follow other cars too closely because:
options: a: You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,b: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.,c: You may not see the road between the cars.
note: Following too closely reduces reaction time, increasing the risk of a collision if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

question: What does double solid yellow lines painted down the middle of the road mean?
options: a: Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b: Railroad crossing ahead.,c: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing from either direction for safety.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,b: A serious traffic safety problem.,c: A minor traffic safety problem.
note: Drinking and driving is a serious safety issue, as even small amounts of alcohol impair driving ability.

question: What happens when you drink coffee after drinking alcohol?
options: a: Decreases blood alcohol concentration BAC.,b: Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration BAC.
note: Coffee does not reduce BAC or counteract alcohol’s impairing effects.

question: Driving under the influence of any medication which impairs your driving is permitted:
options: a: Under no circumstances.,b: If it is prescribed by a doctor.,c: If you don't feel drowsy.
note: Driving under the influence of impairing medication, whether prescription or not, is not permitted.

question: Fines in a construction zone are:
options: a: Cut in half.,b: Tripled.,c: Doubled.
note: Fines in construction zones are typically doubled to deter unsafe driving near workers.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: You should give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a: In any crosswalk or intersection.,b: In a marked crosswalk.,c: Crossing any street.
note: Pedestrians in any crosswalk or intersection have the right-of-way, requiring drivers to yield.

question: Having a driver license is a:
options: a: Right.,b: Privilege.,c: Requirement.
note: A driver’s license is a privilege, not a right, and can be revoked for unsafe behavior.

question: Highway pavement will be particularly dangerous and most slippery when:
options: a: If it has just begun to rain.,b: If it has been raining for several hours.,c: If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: Pavement is most slippery when it has just begun to rain, as oil and water create a slick surface.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a: Replace tires with bad tread.,b: Use tires with proper air pressure.,c: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
note: Avoiding speeding on wet roads reduces the risk of hydroplaning, as does maintaining proper tire tread and pressure.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a: Three,b: Two,c: One
note: Even one alcoholic drink can impair driving ability, affecting reaction time and judgment.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: What should you do if you see a child who is about to run into the street?
options: a: Prepare to slow down.,b: Flash your headlights.,c: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
note: Prepare to slow down to avoid a collision if a child is about to run into the street.

section-name: Interacting with Pedestrians, Bicyclists, and Other Special Road Users
question: What should the motorist do if they see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk?
options: a: Continue ahead as the motorist has the right-of-way.,b: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c: Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.
note: Wait for pedestrians to cross the street, as they have the right-of-way in a crosswalk.

question: What should you do if a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving?
options: a: Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.,b: Pump the brakes rapidly.,c: Grip the steering wheel firmly slow down and exit the traffic lane.
note: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and safely exit the traffic lane to handle a tire blowout.

question: What should you do if an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger?
options: a: Cross the tracks at your own risk.,b: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c: Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed to avoid a collision.

question: What should you do if an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane?
options: a: Use your horn steer right and accelerate.,b: Use your horn steer left and brake.,c: Use your horn steer right and brake.
note: Use your horn to alert the driver, steer right to avoid a collision, and brake to slow down.

question: What should you do if an oncoming headlights are blinding you while you are driving at night?
options: a: Turn your lights on and off.,b: Switch your lights to high beams.,c: Look toward the right edge of the road.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid glare from oncoming headlights.

question: If someone has consumed alcoholic drinks what will help the person overcome the influence of those drinks?
options: a: Tomato juice and lime,b: Hot coffee,c: Fresh air
note: Fresh air and time are the only ways to reduce alcohol’s effects; other substances do not counteract BAC.
